subtype: Approach: search symptoms online and assume the worst [Pitfall]
passage:
Around eleven every night I opened the forums on my phone. A stiffness that came and went had me typing the same words again and again, and each page ended with a frightening name for what I might have. By the third night I was sure, and the rest of the room went silent around me. I stopped sleeping properly, skipped two morning lectures, and told myself I would book a visit once I knew more.

Joseph, my flatmate, found me at the desk at three and asked when I had last eaten. I hadn't booked anything for a week, only read more. Looking back, I had feared a verdict, not gathered facts. Vishal

qa.q: How late did Vishal usually start reading the forums?
What was Vishal feeling by the third night of reading?
qa.a: Vishal was frightened and convinced of the worst, which is why the room seemed to go silent and sleep stopped.

qa.q: What could Vishal try instead of night-time searching, and why?
qa.a: Vishal could book a visit with a doctor and write down the symptoms to discuss, because facts from a professional replace the guesses that grew in the dark.

qa.q: How might Joseph have felt finding Vishal at the desk at three?
qa.a: Joseph was probably worried and a little helpless, seeing a flatmate who was not eating or sleeping and had done nothing but read.

grounding: A student reads forums late at night, assumes the worst, loses sleep and delays a proper visit.

passage:
Team lead's note, 9 October. Indu, customer support.
Vikas has made several errors this week and looks exhausted. Today I asked if he was all right. He said he hadn't slept properly in about ten days.
He told me he'd noticed a small swelling under his jaw a few weeks ago. Instead of seeing a doctor, he had been reading health forums every night, sometimes until 3 a.m. Each thread offered a worse explanation than the last, and by now he was convinced it was something very serious. 'I didn't want to go and hear it,' he said. 'So I kept reading instead.'
I told him I couldn't say what it was, and neither could the forums; only a doctor who examined him could. With his agreement, we booked an appointment at the clinic our insurance covers for tomorrow morning, and I've given him the time off to go.
I'll check in with him after the appointment.

qa.q: Where did Vikas notice a swelling?
Why did Vikas keep reading forums instead of seeing a doctor?
qa.a: He was frightened of hearing bad news, so reading felt safer, even though it fed his worst fears.

qa.q: What could have helped Vikas in the first week he noticed the swelling?
qa.a: Booking a doctor's visit then, and closing the forums at night, so facts replaced late-night guessing.

qa.q: How does the week look to Indu, the team lead who wrote the note?
qa.a: Indu sees errors caused by fear and lost sleep, not carelessness, and helps turn the worry into an appointment.

grounding: Shows a young worker reading forums late at night, assuming the worst about a symptom, losing sleep and delaying a doctor's visit.

passage:
Tuesday, 2:40 a.m. Uday's diary.
Can't sleep, so writing instead. The mole on my left arm looks bigger than I remember. Or I think it does. I started reading about it at 11. Three hours, eleven forums. Every page matches something, and every match is worse than the last. One post had photos I wish I hadn't seen.
My heart is thudding. I've checked the arm under the torch maybe twenty times. I haven't told anyone. I keep thinking if I go to a doctor and they say it, then it's real.
It's been like this for five nights now. Skipped the gym, forgot to return Amma's call, nearly missed a deadline.
Naveen heard me moving and knocked. I showed him. He said, 'You've read everything except a doctor's opinion.' He's booking the skin clinic near the office for me in the morning, and he's coming along.
Maybe I'll sleep now. Maybe not.

qa.q: How many forums did Uday read?
What does Uday checking the arm twenty times suggest?
qa.a: Uday is deeply anxious and frightened, stuck in a loop where each check feeds more fear.

qa.q: What would help Uday more than more reading?
qa.a: Seeing the skin doctor as Naveen arranged, and putting the phone away at night until then.

qa.q: How does Naveen see Uday's night?
qa.a: Naveen sees a friend lost in forums at 2 a.m. and steps in kindly, pointing to the one opinion missing and going along. 🤍

grounding: Shows a young person reading forums late at night, matching a symptom to the worst case, losing sleep and putting off a proper visit.
